chunks: Kamal al-Din: From a group, among them Ali ibn Abdallah al-Warraq, from Abu al-Husayn Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Asadi who said:

… Among what reached me from the Shaykh Abi Ja'far Muhammad ibn Uthman (may God sanctify his soul), in response to my questions to the Master of the Age (peace be upon him): … As for what you asked about regarding the one who prays while the fire, or an image, or a lamp is in front of him – is his prayer permissible? The people differed about this before you, then it is permissible for the one who is not from the descendants of the idol-worshippers or fire-worshippers to pray while the fire, or the image, or the lamp is in front of him, and it is not permissible for the one who is from the descendants of the idol and fire worshippers.
ai.seo_question: Is prayer valid if there is fire or an image in front of the worshipper?
ai.summary: Transmitted via Al-Shaykh al-Mufid's correspondence with Imam al-Zaman, this hadith clarifies a specific fiqh ruling regarding the validity of prayer in the presence of fire, images, or lamps. It introduces a nuanced distinction based on ancestral lineage, prohibiting prayer for descendants of idol or fire worshippers while permitting it for others, reflecting the scholarly tradition of contextualizing ritual purity with historical and genealogical factors.
